name: TerraPraxis: COP26 re-powering event (Founders Pledge)
summary: TerraPraxis promotes re-powering coal plants with advanced nuclear heat. Founders Pledge's Climate Fund paid for its COP26 event on committed coal emissions; Founders Pledge's best guess is $0.02 a tonne of CO₂, $1.10 under conservative assumptions. Like every model on the site, our view uses the evaluator's best guess; the conservative case is the end of the range. Why it is more than ten times its peers: it values one event (an estimated $81,000 grant at COP26), not an organisation's work over years, through three probabilities Founders Pledge guessed; its own conservative case is 55 times lower. We keep the best guess, as for every evaluator.

rows.label: Share of current coal emissions avoided because the event brings re-powering forward

source.title: Founders Pledge, "The ideas of economists" (Climate Fund grants at COP26, Johannes Ackva, 2021)
source.quote: 1 in 10,000 of current coal emissions will be avoided additionally through re-powering five years earlier through the effects of this event,

rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's conservative case lists three items: "There is a 1 in 10,000 chance that", "1 in 10,000 of current coal emissions will be avoided additionally through re-powering five years earlier", and a 1% difference from philanthropic funding. We read the first two as the same 1-in-10,000 factor: taken literally, all three give 7.4 tonnes and an $8 grant. On this reading the best guess (×10 and ×5) reproduces Founders Pledge's $0.02. The linked sheet's oldest tab adds a 0.0001 change to two probabilities ('OLD-Copy of Value of re-powerin'!B5−B4, B10 = 7.4 Mt); it models the IEA grant, not this event.

source.title: Founders Pledge, "The ideas of economists" (Climate Fund grants at COP26, Johannes Ackva, 2021)
source.quote: and that funding this fully philanthropically makes a 1% difference

rows.explainer: Founders Pledge thinks the event would have happened anyway, funded by the nuclear industry or governments; its grant made it independent of self-interest. Its conservative case gives that a 1% difference; its best guess 5%.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂ avoided because of the grant
rows.explainer: Our reading of the page's arithmetic (see the share above): a year's coal emissions × 1 in 10,000, for each of the five years re-powering comes sooner, × the 1% difference the funding made: about 74,000 tonnes.

source.title: Founders Pledge, "The ideas of economists" (Climate Fund grants at COP26, Johannes Ackva, 2021)
source.quote: this would mean you believe that the cost per avoided ton of CO2 would be USD 1.10/tCO2e.

rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's figure under its "extremely conservative" assumptions (the rows above): "USD 1.10/tCO2e". The page doesn't state the grant's size, and the linked sheet models a different TerraPraxis grant (engaging the IEA), so the $1.10 is taken as stated. The evaluator's own subjective guess, filed as a judgment.

rows.label: Grant size implied by the page (cost per tonne × tonnes)
rows.explainer: A check, not used in the result: on our reading the $1.10 implies a grant of about $81,000. Founders Pledge's earlier seed grant to TerraPraxis was $250,000.

rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's best guess for the 1-in-10,000 factor above: 1 in 1,000. The page lists "a 1 in 1000 chance" and "the change it could bring (1 in 1000)"; as in the conservative case, we read the two as one factor.

Cost per tonne of CO₂e avoided, Founders Pledge's best guess (rebuilt)
rows.explainer: The implied grant over the best-guess tonnes: about $0.022, which Founders Pledge rounds to "USD 0.02/tCO2e". So both of Founders Pledge's cases reproduce from the page on our reading.

rows.label: Cost per tonne of CO₂e avoided, Founders Pledge's best guess
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's bottom line, its best guess of $0.02 a tonne, used like every other evaluator's best guess on the site. Its conservative case, $1.10 a tonne, is the high end of the range. The best guess rests on three guessed probabilities for a single event, so the range is wide. The evaluator's own subjective guess, filed as a judgment.

source.title: Founders Pledge, "The ideas of economists" (Climate Fund grants at COP26, Johannes Ackva, 2021)
source.quote: putting our best guess at USD 0.02/tCO2e.

rows.label: Years from the grant until the tonnes are avoided
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's case brings re-powering five years forward; re-powered plants need advanced reactors that are not yet commercial, so the avoided tonnes come in the 2030s or later. Best guess 10 years after the 2021 event, 5 to 20. Our judgment.

rows.label: A marginal dollar's tonnes as a share of the past average (our judgment)
rows.explainer: Our judgment, one figure for every model built on an organisation's past average (facts: meta.marginal_vs_past_average, shared with The Life You Can Save's leverage ratio): the cost per tonne is one past grant (a COP26 event) over its effect, an average; the next dollar does less than the average dollar did, since an organisation pursues its best opportunities first. 50%, from 18% to 100% (average = marginal). The evaluator view keeps 100%.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂e avoided per dollar
rows.explainer: One over the cost per tonne, discounted for the wait until the tonnes are avoided, like every future benefit on the site. A marginal dollar is counted at the shared share of the past average (row above).

rows.label: Share of these tonnes from burning less fuel (coal)
rows.explainer: Re-powering replaces a coal plant's boiler with a clean heat source, so every tonne avoided is coal not burned, and its smoke goes too. The low end allows for some of the re-powered plants' coal being replaced by other fossil fuel elsewhere. Our judgment.

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths per tonne of CO₂ from coal power, relative to the fossil-fuel average

source.title: Markandya & Wilkinson (2007), Electricity generation and health, The Lancet
source.note: Europe, deaths per TWh: coal 24.5. At about 0.82 t CO₂ per MWh that is 0.30 deaths per 10,000 tonnes, 0.20 of the 1.46 average behind the shared rate.

rows.explainer: Per fuel, not the world average. European coal plants cause about 24.5 deaths per TWh (Markandya & Wilkinson 2007), some 0.30 per 10,000 tonnes of CO₂, a fifth of the fossil-fuel average (1.46 per 10,000) behind the site's rate: the low end. The plants re-powering targets are mostly young Asian coal plants with less flue-gas cleaning and denser populations around them, so we double it for the best guess and allow up to the average. Our judgment on that adjustment. Asian-specific mortality per TWh of coal power would firm this up; until then it is a judgment, the third-largest swing in the result.

rows.label: Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne
rows.explainer: The row the site's climate conversion reads (docs/normalization.md 2.5): the air-pollution deaths each of these tonnes avoids, as a multiple of the world average behind the shared rate.

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths averted per tonne, counted directly by the evaluator (none here)
rows.explainer: A row every climate model has, which the site's conversion reads (docs/normalization.md 2.5): air-pollution deaths the evaluator counts itself, per tonne, on top of what the tonnes carry through air_pollution_weight. The evaluator counts none for this charity, so 0.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for research, technical assistance and policy work: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen this charity's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Engineers, analysts and advocates could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂e avoided per dollar you give
rows.explainer: The tonnes per dollar above; with credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash. The site turns these tonnes into years of healthy life through the deaths they avoid ("Deaths caused by one more tonne of CO₂"), heat deaths discounted over the decades until they come, air-pollution deaths at once, scaled by the row above.
